reference_schema.schema_text: Initial state: A harmful incident has affected a victim or valued target, and two or more candidate agents each have some combination of motive, access, or opportunity. The incident was carried out through a method that leaves a discriminating signature: a required credential, specialized tool or permission, controlled inventory item, or object/medication provenance. Goal: select the candidate whose relations explain both why the incident would be committed and how the specific method could actually be executed. Available information: candidate-specific motive; presence or opportunity in the relevant interval; general access; method-specific access; and evidence linking the observed method signature to a candidate's credential, role, tool, inventory, prescription, or controlled object. Constraints: motive, generic scene access, or a superficially similar object alone is insufficient. The decisive method evidence must distinguish one candidate's operational route from an alternative candidate's merely possible route. Solution procedure: identify the method signature; determine what capability, credential, or controlled resource the method required; compare each candidate against that requirement; verify motive and opportunity for the candidate with the strongest method-specific match; and reject a candidate whose motive or generic access lacks the required signature link. Expected outcome: attribute the incident to the candidate for whom motive, opportunity, and method-specific access converge. The mapping package does not provide a numerical evidential threshold, a universal legal standard, or a rule that method evidence is conclusive when multiple candidates match it equally.

roles.description: individual or asset harmed by the incident
one of the alternatives considered responsible for the incident
agent reconstructing responsibility from motive, access, logs, and method evidence
career, reputation, status, financial, or legal loss created by the target's action
mechanism, tool, credentialed operation, or harmful substance used in the incident
broad ability to enter the setting or be present during the relevant interval
role-specific credential, specialized permission, controlled tool, inventory item, or substance access required by the method
trace connecting the actual method to a candidate's distinctive access or controlled resource
candidate with motive or generic access but without an equally strong method-signature match

relations.description: the target's planned action creates a candidate-specific reason to prevent or retaliate against it
the candidate can act in the relevant setting and interval
executing the observed method requires a distinguishing credential, role, tool, inventory source, or controlled substance
the method trace is explained by the candidate's distinctive operational access or controlled resource
motive or broad access without the method-signature link does not uniquely explain the incident
motive and opportunity support responsibility when they converge in the same candidate with the discriminating method-specific link

applicability_conditions.condition: At least two candidate agents have plausible motive, means, access, or opportunity.
The incident method has a trace or operational requirement that can distinguish candidate access.
At least one candidate has method-specific access supported by a credential, controlled item, matching substance, specialized role, or equivalent signature.
The candidate with the method-specific match also has a supported motive and relevant opportunity.
Competing candidates are evaluated under the same motive-access-method criteria rather than eliminated by surface attributes alone.
A physical trace, electronic log, inventory provenance, prescription match, or role-specific operation may instantiate the signature relation.

reference_schema.solution_or_inference_rule: IF multiple candidates have some motive or opportunity, AND the incident method requires a distinguishing credential, capability, controlled resource, or object provenance, AND the observed method signature matches one candidate's method-specific access more directly than the alternatives, AND that same candidate also has a supported motive and relevant opportunity, THEN infer that candidate as the best-supported responsible agent. The logical basis is conjunctive and entity-consistent: motive explains why, opportunity explains when or where, and the signature-access match explains how; all three must converge on the same candidate. A competing candidate's motive, generic access, receipt for a similar object, or possession of broadly related tools is insufficient without an equally specific link to the actual method.
boundaries_and_exceptions: The schema supports comparative attribution, not deductive proof or a legal standard of guilt.
If two candidates have equally strong method-signature links, the schema is insufficient without another discriminating relation.
A similar object is not automatically the incident object; provenance or another operational link must be evaluated.
A credential or controlled resource may have been borrowed, stolen, or misused; such an alternative must be retained when the mapping evidence supports it.
Motive alone and general presence alone are nondiagnostic when shared by multiple candidates.
The mapping package supplies no numerical weights or probability threshold for combining evidence.
Concrete method signatures differ across domains and must not be treated as identical surface attributes.

support.evidence: All selected sources represent multiple suspects with motive/access and distinguish them through method-specific access evidence.
